video_title: ¡Era una PESADILLA! Había partidos que no quería ni jugar | Luis Scola #295

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the power of a player to change a team's history
quotes.excerpt: You have the possibility as a player, with a ball in your hand, to change the history of a team.
quotes.quote: You have the possibility as a player, with a ball in your hand, to change the history of a team. One shot, one second. As a leader, it's much less.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Vos tenés la posibilidad como jugador, de con una pelota en la mano, cambiar la historia de un equipo. Un tiro, un segundo. Como dirigente, muchísimo menos.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on money as a consequence of value creation
quotes.excerpt: I am convinced that money is a consequence. We are not offering anything. Why would they give you a million euros?
quotes.quote: I am convinced that money is a consequence. In fact, when we started in Varese, the argument was 'we have to get money, we have to get money'. And at one point I said, 'Stop. We are not offering anything. Why would they give you a million euros?'
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Estoy convencido que el dinero es una consecuencia. Y de hecho, cuando nosotros empezamos en Varese, el argumento era 'tenemos que conseguir plata, tenemos que conseguir plata'. Y en un momento dije, 'Pará. No estamos ofreciendo nada. ¿Por qué te va a dar un millón de euros?'

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the entrepreneurial nature of being a professional athlete
quotes.excerpt: Being a professional athlete is entrepreneurship. A professional athlete has a small SME, which sometimes becomes a startup.
quotes.quote: Being a professional athlete is entrepreneurship. A professional athlete has a small SME, which sometimes becomes a startup, which sometimes becomes a unicorn of what is their own career. In the United States, they always teach you: be your own brand, take care of your brand, your social media, how you can enlarge it, exploit it, generate value.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Ser deportista profesional es emprender, ¿no? El deportista profesional tiene como una pequeña PYME, que a veces se convierte en una startup, que a veces se convierte en un unicornio de lo que es su propia carrera. De hecho, en Estados Unidos siempre te enseñan: sos tu propio brand, cuidá tu brand, tu social media, esto, lo otro, y cómo podés agrandarlo, explotarlo, generar valor y demás.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the NBA's superior marketing and storytelling
quotes.excerpt: The NBA does a very good job of highlighting you through photos, the aesthetics of their clothes, their courts.
quotes.quote: The NBA does a very good job of highlighting you through photos, the aesthetics of their clothes, their courts, their colors, and how to tell your story in a way that generates things, emotions in people. They are very good at that, they look for that in all players, and they understand that the more of this player I can put out there, the more people will come to watch my game.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: La NBA hace muy bien el tema de realzarte desde las fotos, desde la estética de su ropa, de sus canchas, de sus colores, a cómo contar tu historia de una manera en la cual a la gente le genera cosas, emociones. Son muy buenos para eso, buscan en todos los jugadores eso y entienden como que mientras más de este jugador que yo puedo poner ahí afuera, más la gente va a venir a ver mi partido.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the NBA's focus on player education
quotes.excerpt: The NBA is very good at educating the player, at telling them why they are doing what they are doing.
quotes.quote: The NBA is very good at educating the player, at telling them why they are doing what they are doing. And one is playing here, and here there is not so much spirit. Sport in general is almost a thing of donating money, or giving back to society, or doing something. In contrast, the United States is clearly an entertainment product where you have to sell, you have to buy, you have to spend, you have to promote.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Estados Unidos o la NBA, mejor dicho Estados Unidos, muestra, es muy bueno a educar también al jugador, a contarle por qué está haciendo las cosas que está haciendo. Y uno está jugando acá y acá no hay tanto espíritu, el básquet, el deporte en general es más una cosa, digamos, casi como de de donar plata o de dar devolver a la sociedad o de hacer algo así. En cambio Estados Unidos es claramente un producto de entertainment en donde tenés que vender, tenés que comprar, tenés que gastar, tenés que promover.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on his professional start in Gijón
quotes.excerpt: I had played two years in Argentina, but I lived at home. When I came here, I took a plane.
quotes.quote: I had played two years in Argentina, but I lived at home. I went to school. I wasn't there yet. When I came here, I took a plane, two bags, I lived nearby, they gave me a car, and I got a cell phone. The first time I had a cell phone was that week, and I started a professional career as a foreigner in a professional team that wanted to ascend. I didn't understand what that meant then.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Había jugado dos años en Argentina, pero yo vivía en casa. Iba a la escuela. No no estaba todavía. Cuando me vine acá, me agarré un avión, dos bolsos, vivía acá cerquita, me dieron un auto y me saqué un celular. La primera vez que tuve un teléfono celular fue esa semana y empecé una carrera de profesional como extranjero en un equipo profesional que quería ascender. Yo en la inconsciencia del momento no entendía lo que significa eso.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on dealing with criticism as a young player
quotes.excerpt: I was being criticized from all sides. How can it be? If I am the promise, the future.
quotes.quote: I was being criticized from all sides. How can it be? If I am the promise, the future. Then I understood, I am here, this is what I have to do. It is not something good. I am not surprising anyone, it does not matter what age I have or what future I have. What matters is what I do here, because they hired me for this level of performance.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Me están criticando por todos lados. ¿Cómo puede ser? Si yo soy la promesa, el futuro. Después entendí, yo estoy acá, eso es lo que tengo que hacer. No es algo bueno. No estoy sorprendiendo a nadie, no importa qué edad tenga o qué futuro tenga. Lo que importa es lo que yo hago acá, porque me contrataron para ese nivel de rendimiento.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the NBA's motivational approach
quotes.excerpt: When I arrived in the NBA, someone came to give us one of these motivational talks and said, 'What have you done for me today?'
quotes.quote: When I arrived in the NBA, someone came to give us one of these motivational talks and said, 'What have you done for me today?' And he had it there, put it: 'What have you done for me today?' Don't tell me about yesterday, don't tell me about tomorrow, I don't care. Today, what have you done for me?
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Cuando llegué a la NBA, uno venía a darnos una de estas charlas motivacionales y decía, 'What you have done for me today?' Y lo tenía ahí puesto: 'What you have done for me today?' No me cuentes ayer, no me cuentes mañana, no me interesa. Hoy, ¿qué hiciste por mí?

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the potential of the Chinese basketball market
quotes.excerpt: China was an incredible place for me because I saw some things that are very different.
quotes.quote: China was an incredible place for me because I saw some things that are very different, that open your mind a lot more. Obviously, at the development level, it is very far behind the NBA, the EuroLeague, and a lot of things. But it has a particularity that I did not find in any other place, which is that its potential is very high.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: China fue un lugar increíble para mí porque vi unas cosas muy diferentes, que te abren la cabeza un montón más. Obviamente, a nivel desarrollo está muy por por detrás que la NBA, que la Euroliga, que un montón de cosas. Pero tiene una particularidad que no encontré en otro lugar, que es que su potencial es altísimo.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on his transition to club management in Varese
quotes.excerpt: There is an entrepreneur there, very important, Antonio Bulgheroni, Toto Bulgheroni, who is the one who calls me.
quotes.quote: There is an entrepreneur there, very important, Antonio Bulgheroni, Toto Bulgheroni, who is the one who calls me. He had played in the club many years ago, won a couple of EuroLeagues, had undertaken, it had gone very well, he had bought the club, then he had sold it, and now he had returned as a counselor. He calls me, tells me his story, I thought it was a fascinating story.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hay un emprendedor ahí muy importante, Antonio Bulgheroni, Toto Bulgheroni, que es quien me llama. Él había jugado en el club hace muchos años, ganado un par de Euroligas, había emprendido, le había ido muy bien, había comprado el club, después lo había vendido, y ahora había vuelto como consejero. Me llama, me cuenta su historia, me pareció una historia fascinante.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on his process for creating value in Varese
quotes.excerpt: We want to do, I don't know, the Abanomenti campaign. Okay, we call a friend from Indiana.
quotes.quote: We want to do, I don't know, the Abanomenti campaign. Okay, we call a friend from Indiana. 'How...?' 'Yes, I don't know what...' And do you have any documents? 'Yes, yes, because yesterday we had the meeting.' 'Can't you pass it to me? I have to...' Email, so I took it, printed it, took the Indiana Pacer, put the logo for Varese, changed it to yellow, put it red, translated it to Italian, and sent it.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Queremos hacer, no sé, la campaña de abanomenti. Okay, llamamos a algún amigo de Indiana, ¿cómo...? Sí, no sé qué y vos tenés algún documento. Sí, sí, porque ayer tuvimos la reunión. ¿No me lo pasás? Que tengo que... Email, entonces yo agarraba, lo imprimía, agarraba Indiana Pacer, ponía el logo para que Varese, le cambiaba el amarillo, lo ponía rojo, lo traducía al italiano y lo mandaba.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the fast pace of basketball vs. management
quotes.excerpt: Playing basketball is very fast, very... everything happens in a week, in a game, in a day.
quotes.quote: Playing basketball is very fast, very... everything happens in a week, in a game, in a day, in a shot. You have the possibility as a player, with a ball in your hand, to change the history of a team, of a whole society. Well, here we played a game and Jordi Millera, one who played in Manresa, took a free throw, and if he made it, we went down. If the Varese basketball is there, he took it from that hoop that was there.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Jugar al básquet es muy rápido, muy... todo pasa en una semana, en un partido, en un día, en un tiro. Vos tenés la posibilidad como jugador, de con una pelota en la mano, cambiar la historia de un equipo, de una sociedad entera. Bueno, acá jugamos un partido y Jordi Millera, uno que jugaba en Manresa, tiró un tiro libre y si lo metía descendíamos. Si el Varese básquet está ahí, lo tiró desde ese aro que estaba ahí.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the slow pace of club management
quotes.excerpt: I know that we are going much slower than you think we have to go, but we are going much faster.
quotes.quote: I know that we are going much slower than you think we have to go, but we are going much faster than you think we have to go. Things happen much slower, they happen from month to month, they don't happen day by day, they don't happen from minute to minute, from action to action.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Sé que estamos yendo mucho más lento de lo que vos creés que tenemos que ir, pero estamos yendo mucho más rápido de lo que nosotros creemos que tenemos que ir. Las cosas pasan mucho más lento, pasan de mes a mes, no pasan de día a día, no pasan de minuto a minuto, de acción a acción.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the human resistance to change
quotes.excerpt: The human being always resists change. When you want to change things, the comfort of the people.
quotes.quote: The human being always resists change. When you want to change things, the comfort of the people is usually complicated to change. It is habitual.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: El ser humano siempre se resiste al cambio. Cuando querés cambiar las cosas, la comodidad de la gente suele ser complicado de cambiar. Es habitual.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on money as a consequence of value creation
quotes.excerpt: I am convinced that money is a consequence. We are not offering anything. Why would they give you a million euros?
quotes.quote: I am convinced that money is a consequence. In fact, when we started in Varese, the argument was 'we have to get money, we have to get money'. And at one point I said, 'Stop. We are not offering anything. Why would they give you a million euros?' You have to create value.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Estoy convencido que el dinero es una consecuencia. Y de hecho, cuando nosotros empezamos en Varese, el argumento era 'tenemos que conseguir plata, tenemos que conseguir plata'. Y en un momento dije, 'Pará. No estamos ofreciendo nada. ¿Por qué te va a dar un millón de euros?' Vos tenés que crear valor.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on building Varese's youth program
quotes.excerpt: We put a whole youth sector. We didn't have a youth sector, it was outsourced. We took it.
quotes.quote: We put a whole youth sector. We didn't have a youth sector, it was outsourced. We took it. We went from zero to 450. We started to do, first, a lot of hard work for the key points of the city, communes, press, sponsorships, etc., to explain who we were and what we wanted to do.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Pusimos todo un sector juvenil. No teníamos sector juvenil, estaba tercerizado. Lo agarramos. Pasamos de cero a 450. Empezamos a hacer, primero, todo un trabajo de hormiga por los puntos claves de la ciudad, comunas, prensa, patrocinios, etcétera, a explicarles quiénes éramos y qué queríamos hacer.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the importance of passion in entrepreneurship
quotes.excerpt: There is a common thing of people who undertake successfully. It is that passion for what they are doing.
quotes.quote: There is a common thing of people who undertake successfully. It is that passion for what they are doing. The passion per se does not give you anything. What the passion gives you is that you are walking down the street and you are thinking. You are thinking about the clothes, about this, about that. I am thinking about the club, about the player, about the...
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hay una cosa común de la gente que emprende exitosamente. Es esa pasión por lo que está haciendo. La pasión per se no te da nada. Lo que te da la pasión es eso de que vos estás caminando por la calle y estás pensando. Vos estarás pensando en la ropa, en esto, en lo otro. Yo estoy pensando en el club, en el jugador, en el...

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on his internal dialogue and passion
quotes.excerpt: I already talked to the mirror, walking, running, with the headphones, on the plane. I already talked.
quotes.quote: I already talked to the mirror, walking, running, with the headphones, on the plane. I already talked, inside my head, and when you have that thing of internal dialogue, then it comes out in another way. And when it comes out with that conviction, it convinces.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Yo ya lo hablé con el espejo, caminando, corriendo, con los auriculares, en el avión. Yo ya lo hablé, dentro de mi cabeza, y cuando vos tenés esa cosa de diálogo interno, después sale de otra manera. Y cuando sale con esa convicción, convence.

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on Elon Musk's disruptive impact
quotes.excerpt: Elon Musk changes the world four or five times. He goes, does PayPal, sells it.
quotes.quote: Elon Musk changes the world four or five times. He goes, does PayPal, sells it. In 90% of mortals, they go to Margarita Island and you don't see them anymore. No, he bets everything and is going to make an electric car, which was... if an industry, let's say, of the most difficult is the industry of banks, the second, surely, is the oil industry, of the naphtha, and the guy went against that. And he wins, and does what he does. And then he wants to take rockets and go to Mars, and then he wants to make solar panels, and then...
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Elon Musk cambia el mundo cuatro o cinco veces. Va, hace PayPal, lo vende. En el 90% de los mortales, se va a la isla Margarita y no lo ves más. No, él apuesta todo y se va a hacer un auto eléctrico, que era la... si una industria, digamos, de las más difíciles es la industria de los bancos, la segunda, seguramente, es la industria petrolera, de la nafta, y el tipo fue contra eso. Y gana, y hace lo que hace. Y después se quiere llevar cohetes e ir a Marte, y después quiere hacer paneles solares, y después...

quotes.speaker: Luis Scola
quotes.summary_phrase: Luis Scola on the mental toll of the Olympic qualification process
quotes.excerpt: I took that fight seriously and I did it very intensely.
quotes.quote: I fought against aging a lot. I said, okay, I am going to age, I am going to disappear like it happens to everyone, but I am going to fight. I am going to make it as difficult as possible, and I took that fight seriously and I did it very intensely. Obviously, I ended up losing like everyone else, and I took it to a point that was difficult to sustain.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Yo luché contra eso mucho. Yo dije, okay, yo voy a envejecer, yo voy a desaparecer como le pasa a todo el mundo, pero voy a pelear. Se lo voy a poner lo más difícil posible y me tomé esa pelea en serio y lo hice muy intensamente. Después, obviamente, la terminé perdiendo como todo el mundo y la llevé a un punto que era difícil de sostener.
